title: Supported Kummer projective-line decomposition, trace and open counit across sites
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data of [def-pur-conventions], put $A=A_{E,n}$ with $n\geq1$, and let $S$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], without assuming $S$ separated over $k$. For every scheme $T$ used below, work in the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on its small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with comparison $C_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] and derived tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$, write $L_{T,r}=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^r,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_T$, and use the root-projection comparison $C_TL_{T,r}\cong A_T(1)$ and its tensor powers [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent, def-coefficient-twists-detailed].
Let $q:P=\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ and $i:S\hookrightarrow P$ be the infinity divisor $H$, with $\mathcal O_P(H)=\mathcal O_P(1)$. Let $b_q^e:L_{S,r}[2]\oplus A_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{e,*}L_{P,r}[2]$, $h_q^e:A_S\to Rq_{e,*}L_{P,r}[2]$, and $t_q^e=\operatorname{pr}_2(b_q^e)^{-1}$ be the ordinary Kummer-normalized maps [def-amb-p1-trace]. On the pro-etale site let $h_q^p$ be the adjunct of $A_P\to i_*A_S\xrightarrow{c_{H,A}}A_P(1)[2]$, using the supported Cartier class [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], and let $b_q^p$ have components the shifted twisted unit and $h_q^p$; these are the arrows $h^p$, $u^p$ and $b^p=[u^p,h^p]$ of [def-pur-supported-projective-chern, def-pur-supported-projective-site-arrows] in the finite site coordinates of [def-pur-finite-site-coordinates] (these definition nodes index the coefficient ring as $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n'+1}$ and the exponent by $\ell^{r'+1}A=0$; take $n'=n-1$, $r'=r-1$). Under the specified tensor, shift and biproduct comparisons, the counit-mate $\beta_q$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] satisfies
$$\beta_qC_S(h_q^e)=h_q^p,\qquad \beta_qC_S(b_q^e)=b_q^p.$$
The map $b_q^p$ is invertible, and $t_q^p=\operatorname{pr}_2(b_q^p)^{-1}$, the projective trace of [def-pur-supported-projective-site-arrows], satisfies $t_q^p\beta_q=C_S(t_q^e)$ and $t_q^ph_q^p=1$.
For every open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ between finite-type $k$-schemes, the canonical $e_j:C_Tj_!^e\cong j_!^pC_U$ of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], taken on complexes as in [def-pur-open-site-comparison-arrows], identifies the actual derived counits $j_!j^*\to1$ under the canonical inverse-image comparisons. In particular for $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow P$, $\beta_q$ and $e_j$ identify the composites $Rq_*j_!j^*L_{P,r}[2]\to Rq_*L_{P,r}[2]\xrightarrow{t_q^e}A_S$ and $Rq_*j_!j^*A_P(1)[2]\to Rq_*A_P(1)[2]\xrightarrow{t_q^p}A_S$.

proof.text: The hypotheses required by the ordinary decomposition and the comparison mate hold on this domain. The spectrum of a field is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and the unit ideal), so finite type over $k$ makes $S$ Noetherian. The projective projection $q$ is proper, hence finite type and separated; finite type includes quasi-compactness, and separatedness implies quasi-separatedness. Moreover $\ell\neq p$ by the conventions, and $p=0$ in $\mathcal O_S$ because $S$ is a $k$-scheme, so $\ell$, hence $N=\ell^r$, is invertible on $S$ and on every $S$-scheme; this is the invertibility required by the ordinary decomposition, the projective-site arrows, the supported Cartier lemma and finite Tate descent. Thus the ordinary decomposition applies with $N=\ell^r$, and the canonical direct-image mate is invertible on $L_{P,r}[2]$. This sheaf shifted by $2$ is bounded below; only this bounded-below instance of direct-image comparison will be used. None of these hypotheses requires $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to be separated.

proof.text:
Put $K=L_{P,r}[2]$ and $a:C_Pq_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}q_p^*C_S$. The transpose of $\beta_{q,K}C_S(h_q^e)$ is
$$\varepsilon^p_{C_PK}\,q_p^*(\beta_{q,K})\,q_p^*C_S(h_q^e)
=C_P(\varepsilon^e_K)a^{-1}_{Rq_{e,*}K}q_p^*C_S(h_q^e)
=C_P(\varepsilon^e_Kq_e^*h_q^e)a^{-1}_{A_S}
=C_P(x^e)a^{-1}_{A_S}=x^p.$$
The first equality is precisely the counit normalization of the named comparison mate; the second is naturality of $a$. Both adjunction transposes are bijections, by the mate conventions. Since $h_q^p$ is defined as the transpose of $x^p$, this proves $\beta_qC_S(h_q^e)=h_q^p$ for the specified arrows.

The first component is also preserved. Apply the mate-unit identity to $q_e^*\dashv Rq_{e,*}$, $q_p^*\dashv Rq_{p,*}$, $G=C_S$, $H=C_P$, and $\alpha=a^{-1}$. It gives
$$\beta_{q,q_e^*M}C_S(\eta^e_M)=Rq_{p,*}(a_M^{-1})\eta^p_{C_SM}.$$
Take $M=L_{S,r}[2]$ and use the canonical finite Tate pullback identification $q_e^*M=L_{P,r}[2]$. Its site comparison is the one furnished by finite Tate descent. The right side is the shifted twisted unit $u^p$, with exactly this target identification. Thus $\beta_qC_S(u^e)=u^p$. Exactness of $C$ supplies its additive biproduct and shift comparisons. This is implemented directly with Adjunction.homEquiv_unit and homEquiv naturality, so the separate mate-unit-compatibility statement is unnecessary.

The maps from the two summands determine a map out of their biproduct. Steps 3 and 4 therefore give $\beta_qC_S(b_q^e)=b_q^p$. Since $b_q^e$ and $\beta_q$ are isomorphisms, so is $b_q^p$. Here only the arrows $h^p,u^p,b^p$ in the projective-site definition are used; its assertion of invertibility is established by this argument, rather than assumed.

Under the biproduct comparison, the second projection is $C_S(\operatorname{pr}_2)$. Inverting the identity of Step 5 gives
$$(b_q^p)^{-1}\beta_q=C_S((b_q^e)^{-1}),$$
so multiplication by the second projection proves $t_q^p\beta_q=C_S(t_q^e)$. Also $h_q^p=b_q^p\iota_2$, hence $t_q^ph_q^p=\operatorname{pr}_2\iota_2=1$. These are equalities for the inverse-decomposition trace prescribed in the statement.

We verify the open counit first on sheaves. Write $r=j_e^*$, $s=j_p^*$, $e=j_!^e$, $d=j_!^p$, $a:C_Ur\cong sC_T$, $c:C_Te\cong dC_U$. The existing unit-normalization statement for this particular $c$ is $s(c_F)a_{eF}C_U(\eta^e_F)=\eta^d_{C_UF}$. For an etale sheaf $B$ put $g=C_T(\varepsilon^e_B)c_{rB}^{-1}:dC_UrB\to C_TB$. Its $d\dashv s$ transpose is
$$s(g)\eta^d_{C_UrB}=sC_T(\varepsilon^e_B)a_{erB}C_U(\eta^e_{rB})=a_B C_U(r\varepsilon^e_B\,\eta^e_{rB})=a_B.$$
The middle equality is naturality and the last is the triangle identity. The transpose of $\varepsilon^p_{C_TB}d(a_B)$ is also $a_B$. Equality under the adjunction bijection gives
$$C_T(\varepsilon^e_B)=\varepsilon^p_{C_TB}d(a_B)c_{rB}.$$
This proves the required normalization for the canonical extension comparison, not for a newly chosen isomorphism. Reuse the existing proved derived-unit-normalization helper comparison_derived_extension_mate; a general counit_of_unit calculation applies the same naturality and triangle identities directly in the unbounded derived categories.

Both open extensions by zero are exact, and both restrictions are exact constant-ring inverse images. The comparison inverse images are exact as well. Consequently the sheaf identity of Step 7 applies degree by degree to any complex, with no boundedness restriction. By the exact-derived-adjunction convention, the actual units and counits of $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$ are precisely the localized degreewise units and counits. Localizing the equality therefore yields the claimed equality of actual derived counits. The open comparison defined in the item is exactly this termwise $c$, descended to derived categories, so it is the named $e_j$. Its degreewise localization is already supplied by that derived-unit helper. Expand the exact-derived restriction coordinate isomorphisms and cancel their inverse/hom pairs; extension-comparison naturality then gives the exact source comparison in the statement.

proof.text:
Finally take $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow P$ and $K=L_{P,r}[2]$, and let $v^e:j_!^ej_e^*K\to K$ be its counit. Write $E:C_Pj_!^ej_e^*K\cong j_!^pj_p^*C_PK$ for the composite of $e_j$ and the inverse-image comparison. Step 8 says $C_P(v^e)=v^pE$. Naturality of the direct-image mate and Step 6 then give
$$t_q^pRq_{p,*}(v^p)Rq_{p,*}(E)\beta_{q,j_!^ej_e^*K}
=t_q^p\beta_{q,K}C_S(Rq_{e,*}v^e)
=C_S(t_q^e Rq_{e,*}v^e).$$
The source comparison is invertible: $j_!^ej_e^*K$ is bounded below by exactness in Step 8, so it lies in the mate's stated domain. Finite Tate descent identifies $C_PK$ with $A_P(1)[2]$. This is the stated comparison of the two composites, with every source identification displayed.
